note: The Round Trip table: ONE ROW PER BRIEF LEG FIELD (kogaki#1013/#1014).
`field` names the Brief Leg field the Reverse Outline side is read from, under
the Brief's own name and definition. It replaces the translation column, which was a
TRANSLATION COLUMN between the Brief and a second schema for the same
information — that schema is deleted, so what the column translated between no
longer has two sides. Where `field` and `declared_block` read the same, that is
the round trip: the same field, forward and reverse.
THE HYGIENE AND MOVE ROWS ARE GONE, and their removal is the ruling rather than
a trim (owner, 2026-09-09). Prose hygiene is not part of Reverse Outlining: a
reader cannot infer the source a structure was produced from, and being able to
would be abnormal. So exemplar-leak, packet-wording, term-before-introduction
and restates-earlier-leg left the table. move-contract left with them because
the Move is not in the Reverse Outline at all — supplying the candidates would
make the outcome ride on supplied information, and the Move's effect is carried
by the reader states, which ARE compared. Whether any of the five survives as a
realization-time lint in `draft` is a separate question for the owner.
`register-tests` LEFT THE TABLE FOR THE SAME REASON, one ruling later
(owner, 2026-09-11). It was the last prose lint standing: its declared side
was the Packet's write-instruction paragraph and its reverse side was the
passage itself, so no Reverse Outline field was involved at all. In the
first full run it failed on seven of eight Legs, every time on "one
relation per sentence", and sent nothing to correction -- a best-effort row
that fires on almost every Leg reports the register of the prose, not a
reconstruction gap. Whether register lints return at realization time inside
`draft` stays the open question the paragraph above already records; it is
the same question for this row.
AND `already-knows` GAINS A `when_declared_absent` ARM in the same act. Its
declared side is the Packet's `already knows` list, which is EMPTY for the
first Leg of every article by construction, and the pair was rendered
anyway: the model was asked whether the passage re-introduced a term the
reader already knew, over a list of no terms, and returned `fails` with a
reason stating the opposite -- that the passage introduces both terms for
the first time. `claims` and `introduces` already carry such an arm and
reach the same runtime branch, so this is one table entry and no second
mechanism.
THE CLAIMS ITEM ASKS ABOUT RECOVERY, AND THREE ROWS LEFT THE TABLE WITH THAT
RULING (owner, 2026-09-17; kogaki#1132).
`claims` USED TO ASK THE WRONG QUESTION. It was `paired`: each outlined claim
was matched to the declared claim it shared the most words with, and the Judge
was asked, once per OUTLINED claim, whether that claim asserted no more than
the declared ones license. The Packet renders Journey material under "NOT a
claim to recover" and tells the writer to retell it, so a correctly realized
passage asserts more than its declared claim BY DESIGN — and on the first full
run the item failed on five of five Legs in both passes, five of the six
residue lines in one article. Reverse Outlining asks one thing here: can the
reader recover what the Leg declared. So the Judge is asked once per DECLARED
claim whether that claim is present among what the reader wrote, surplus is
ignored, and whether a paraphrase counts is the Judge's answer in words and
never a shared-word count — which is why `outlined_claim_containment` left the
thresholds with the matcher that read it.
`claims-unused` IS THE SAME ITEM AND IS NOW INSIDE IT. It was the best-effort
mechanical row reporting a declared claim no outlined claim matched, and it
held on every Leg of that run: the item with a consequence detected surplus,
and the item that detected a lost claim had none. With declared A and B and
outlined A' and A'', both matching A, `claims` held twice, `claims-unused`
failed, and B's loss was never named to the correction. ONE preserved item now
carries both halves, once per declared claim.
`concession` AND `section-continues` LEFT THE TABLE, and neither read a Brief
field. `concession` entered through kogaki#871's body on 2026-09-04 with no
design-table row and no later approval. `section-continues` asked whether a
continuing passage restates its heading — a realization lint of the class
removed on 2026-09-09, and the heading is rendered by the Harness from the
trace, so whether a Leg opens a Section is never information the prose has to
carry. `concession` and `opens_section` leave the Blind Reader's fields with
them, which become five: `purpose`, `reader_state_before`,
`reader_state_after`, `claims`, `introduces`. The `section_placement` Packet
block leaves `packet_blocks` with its one reader, as `register_tests` did at
kogaki#1098.
The comparison's ITEM TABLE, fixed in the Harness (kogaki#872).
WHICH PACKET INFORMATION MUST BE RECONSTRUCTIBLE IS DECIDED ONCE, HERE, per
item class — and the judging model never assigns one. It answers one
question about one pair and returns one of three tokens. src/review-draft.mjs
READS this file rather than restating it, the same arrangement
one edit and never a two-copy divergence.
`class` IS THE CONSEQUENCE, not a severity. A Leg is sent to correction only
on a `fails` in a PRESERVED item; a best-effort fail rides along when that
Leg is re-realized anyway. There is no score, no ranking and no aggregate —
the three tokens are the whole vocabulary, and `cannot-decide` is never
rounded to either neighbour.
`mode` IS WHO DECIDES, and it is the half that keeps the model out of the
mechanical items:
- `mechanical` — the Harness decides from string facts about the Draft and
the Packet. NO join Packet is rendered and no model call is made.
- `judged`     — the Harness renders one join Packet (the declared line,
the outlined line, the quoted span, one question) and records the
verdict that comes back.
- `per-declared` — the Harness renders ONE join Packet PER DECLARED
ENTRY: that entry alone on the declared side, everything the reader
wrote for the field on the reverse, and one question asking whether the
declared entry is among what they wrote. The row fails when ANY entry
fails, and the failing entry carries the declared text that was lost, so
the correction is told WHICH thing went missing rather than only that the
row failed. Surplus on the reverse side is not judged at all.
`declared_block` names the Packet block the declared side is read from, and
src/review-draft.mjs refuses BY NAME when a Packet carries no such block —
a missing block is a PACKET GAP filed against src/packet-template.md, per
the owner's 2026-09-04 closed-input ruling, and never something the
comparison works around.
NOT COMPARED, enumerated so a reader can tell a boundary from a hole:
rationale, materials, reader_state_before, and the thesis and reader target
per Leg.
THE ARTICLE LEVEL IS NOBODY'S HERE (owner, 2026-09-17; kogaki#1133). It was
the cold reader's: kogaki#873 added a Section ledger and five Section pairs
to this table, and they are gone with the reader that answered them. Reverse
Outlining reconstructs the elements of a LEG, and the thesis is not a Leg
element -- of those five pairs the heading was preserved trivially by the
Harness that renders it, three duplicated the reader-state items one level
up, and the thesis pair, the one check no Leg item made, had no act in
ReviewDraft at all, because corrections are Leg-level and a thesis fail
could only ever become residue saying the Packets lack something. That is a
Brief-time finding. So `sections`, `ledger_fields` and `final_claim_field`
left this file, and `thesis` and `opening_question` left `packet_blocks`
with their only reader, as `section_placement` did at kogaki#1098.
THE REOPEN TRIGGER, NAMED so a later reader can tell a ruling from an
omission: a Draft whose every Leg holds the round trip and whose thesis the
owner cannot find on reading it. If that happens the check is designed at
BRIEF COMPOSITION, where the chain of `reader_state_after` values should
reach the thesis, as an operation outside the Reverse Outlining item set --
and never as a sixth row here.
THE FIGURE HALF IS BACK, RESTATED AGAINST THE RECORD'S OWN FIELDS
(kogaki#1018). It left this table at kogaki#1014 under a recorded decline: its
five rows read a reverse side out of the second schema that act deleted, and
the Blind Reader returns a Brief Leg block, which carries no such field.
WHAT REPLACED IT IS THE PASSAGE'S OWN RULE, ONE ARTIFACT DOWN. A passage is
written from a Brief Leg, so its Reverse Outline is a Brief Leg block; a
figure is written from its RECORD, so its Reverse Outline is a block in the
fields src/figure-schema.json declares. There is no second schema at either
level, which is the property kogaki#1014 landed and this is that property for
the figure.
THE DISPOSITION RULE IS THE SAME RULE. `element`, `caption` and `position` are
reconstructible and COMPARED -- a reader who met the rendered block can say
each of them. `kind`, `relations` and `emphasis` are not reconstructible and
are REFUSED rather than merely unasked: the kind and the relations are the
Move form's, and a reader cannot infer the form a structure was produced from.
IT IS ITS OWN FENCE AND ITS OWN FILE. `figure` IS a Brief Leg field and is
declared not reconstructible, so a `figure:` line inside the passage's outline
stays refused; one file per vocabulary is what keeps either reading from
acquiring a key belonging to the other.
`figure_only: true` marks a row that exists only for a Leg whose trace entry
carries a figure. On a Leg without one the row is not evaluated, not rendered
and NOT LOGGED -- a vacuous `holds` for every figureless Leg would put a
figure line in a Draft that has no figure. `record_field` is to the figure
record what `declared_block` is to the Packet, and `figure_field` names the
line read back out of the figure's own Reverse Outline. A row naming both
`field` and `figure_field` is refused: that pair would be a translation
between the Brief's names and the record's, which is the column this chain
removed.
NOW COMPARED, and enumerated so a reader can tell a boundary from a hole:
the figure's elements, its caption, its element-to-claim binding, its reading
against the prose, and its position -- five rows, three preserved and two best-effort, on the same three verdicts and the same consequence rule.
THE PACKET'S LAYOUT IS DATA, not a literal in the runtime (kogaki#872).
src/review-draft.mjs reads a declared block by its KIND, and every label,
heading and fixed instruction sentence the reader keys on lives here. Two
things follow, and the second is the reason:
- amending src/packet-template.md is one edit here and never a hunt
through the comparison for a string that used to match;
- the runtime carries no literal that HAPPENS to equal a field name
somewhere else. `claims`, `purpose` and `reader_state_after` are
each a Packet label AND an item id AND (for two of them) an outlined
record field, and a runtime spelling them out cannot be told apart
from one restating the table or the schema. A synonym in a join key
is the same defect as a divergence.
`after_words` is the template's own fixed instruction paragraph, matched
as a WORD SEQUENCE so a rewrap — which changes nothing — does not silently
hand the instruction back as the block's value.
`claims`'s prefix carries a LEADING `\s*` (the relations layer, kogaki#1174).
A claim the Brief marks a satellite renders one level indented, under its
nucleus, and the prefix that locates a claim line must still match it there
— a bare `claim:` anchored at column zero would silently drop every
satellite claim from the comparison, which is a hole nothing here would
notice.

move_excerpt.heading: An exemplar of this Move — FORM ONLY
move_excerpt.after_words: Read it for the form of the movement and nothing else.

note: THE SECOND PASS'S BOUND IS DATA, for the reason the packet_blocks
note gives one block down (kogaki#874). `check` re-judges the
corrected Legs' own items, the CONTINUITY items on the Leg
immediately after each correction, and every mechanical item over
the whole Draft -- and the runtime names none of those ids, because
an item id spelled out in the runtime cannot be told from one
restating this table.
`successor_items` IS ONE id, and it was two (kogaki#1014). The issue
named two properties the successor carries -- `reader_state_before`
continuity and `restates`. The first is `already-knows`: no LEG item
reads the Packet's `reader_state_before` slot, and the block carrying
the reader's INCOMING state on the Leg side is `already_knows`. The
second was `restates-earlier-leg`, and that row left the table with
the hygiene rows -- a reader cannot infer the source a structure was
produced from -- so the property has no item to be re-checked on. It is
recorded here rather than dropped silently: the successor arm now
re-checks incoming-state continuity alone, and whether the restates
property returns as a realization-time lint in `draft` is the separate
question that removal left open.
NARROWED AT kogaki#873 AND UN-NARROWED AT kogaki#1133. The clause read
`this table declares NO reader for it`, flatly; the Section pair
`section-belief-before` read exactly that block, so the sentence was
narrowed to the LEG items it had always been arguing about. That pair
left with the cold reader, and the flat reading is true again --
recorded here rather than silently restored, because a reader who
remembers the narrowing should be able to see what removed it.
`drift_blocks` are the Packet blocks the drift measure reports
verbatim overlap against -- the claim and state lines. Same
arrangement, same reason.
THE FIGURE ROWS ARE BACK IN THE TABLE (kogaki#1018) AND STILL ADD NO ARM
HERE. They added none while they were here before, they removed none by
leaving, and they add none returning: the second pass's arms are the
corrected Legs' own items, the successor's continuity item and every
mechanical item, and a figure row is reached by whichever of those its
Leg is in. `figure-element-claim` is mechanical, so it is in the third
arm over the whole Draft; the judged figure rows are in the first on a
corrected Leg exactly as that Leg's other rows are. NO FIGURE ROW IS A
SUCCESSOR ITEM: a correction moves the prose the NEXT Leg continues
from, and it moves no figure.
Thresholds are INPUTS TO THE HARNESS AND NEVER OUTPUT. No emitted line
carries one — a comparison line renders line numbers and nothing else
numeric, so a reader cannot mistake a tuning constant for evidence.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Leg declares no claim, so there is nothing for the reader to have recovered and the question below quantifies over nothing; what the passage asserts is judged by the Leg's other items

items.question: The declared claim is above, in the words the Leg declares it in, and below it is every claim this reader wrote down after reading the passage blind. Is that declared claim among them? Answer `holds` where one of the claims the reader wrote says it — a paraphrase counts, and the wording need not match; answer `fails` where no claim they wrote carries it, which means the passage did not put it in front of the reader. What the reader wrote BEYOND the declared claim is not yours to judge here: the Leg is told to retell material it asserts nothing about, so surplus is expected and this question is about recovery alone.

The declared side above renders this Leg's claims as a TREE (the relations layer, kogaki#1174): a claim indented under another, marked `— satellite (<relation>)`, is a satellite of the claim directly above it at the shallower indent. Read the passage below. For every satellite the tree above declares, is it realized FUSED into a clause or phrase of the sentence carrying its nucleus — never as a sentence or paragraph standing on its own? Answer `holds` where every satellite is fused this way, or where the tree above declares no satellite at all — there is nothing to check. Answer `fails` where a satellite is realized as its own paragraph, apart from its nucleus, naming which one.

Does the state this passage assumes a reader arrives in match the state the Forward Artifact declares they arrive in? Answer `fails` where the passage assumes the reader already holds something the declared arriving state does not give them, or re-establishes something it does.
Do the declared reader state and the outlined one describe the same reader? Answer `fails` if a reader in the outlined state would not be in the declared one.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Leg's Packet says to introduce no term, so the question below quantifies over nothing, and a passage that introduces nothing carries no `introduces:` line to read against it

items.question: Is every term the Packet says to introduce here actually introduced in this passage — usable by the reader afterwards? Answer `fails` if a declared term is used without being made usable, or is not present at all.
Do the declared purpose and the outlined one name the same job for this Leg? Answer `fails` if the passage is doing a different job.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Leg's Packet lists no term the reader already knows, so there is nothing for the passage to re-introduce and the question below quantifies over nothing

items.question: Does the passage re-introduce a term the reader already knows — explaining again what an earlier Leg established? Answer `fails` if it does.

Every element the record declares is above, with the wording it was given. Can a reader name each of them from the figure as it was rendered? Answer `fails` if an element the record declares is not among the ones the reader named. This asks about presence, never about how well an element is worded.

The declared side carries the record's caption and the state the Leg says its reader is left in. Does what the reader holds after looking at the figure agree with both? Answer `fails` if it agrees with neither, or if it agrees with the caption while the caption and the Leg's state pull apart.

Both sides here were read blind, from the passage and the figure the reader met beside it. Do the figure and the prose of this Leg say the same thing? Answer `fails` if the figure asserts something the passage does not, or the other way about.

The declared side says whether the figure was designed to set the passage up or to discharge it, and the reverse side is where the reader says they met it. The figure's draft line numbers in the prose below say where it actually sits. Did the reader meet it where the prose needed it? Answer `fails` if the passage had already done the work the figure was meant to set up, or still needed the figure it had not yet been given.
